model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity of different blocks across a sequence of indices, categorized into two distinct groups. The horizontal category axis is labeled "Block Index" and sequentially orders discrete integer indices from left to right, with major tick marks visibly labeled at 0, 15, 31, 47, and 63. The vertical value axis is labeled "Sensitivity" and employs a logarithmic scale, featuring major tick marks annotated at $10^{-5}$ and $10^{-4}$, which correspond to light dashed horizontal gridlines spanning the chart, alongside unannotated minor logarithmic tick marks. The vertical axis range extends from roughly $10^{-6}$ at the bottom to slightly above $10^{-4}$ at the top. A legend in the upper left corner indicates the color coding for the two categories: "4-Fbit" is represented by blue bars, and "2-Fbit" is represented by green bars. Rather than grouping or stacking multiple bars at each index, the chart displays a single bar per block index, assigned to one of the two color-coded categories. There are approximately 64 consecutive bars plotted in total. The shortest bar is located near block index 5, colored green (2-Fbit), with a sensitivity value of approximately $1.5 \times 10^{-6}$. The tallest bar is found near the end of the sequence at index 62, colored blue (4-Fbit), reaching a peak sensitivity slightly above $2 \times 10^{-4}$. Green (2-Fbit) bars primarily occupy the lower to middle indices (such as from index 0 to 26), with sensitivity values generally fluctuating between $2 \times 10^{-6}$ and $2 \times 10^{-5}$. Blue (4-Fbit) bars appear in discrete clusters in the middle of the chart and continuously dominate the upper block indices (from index 49 to 63, barring a single green bar at index 53), displaying values that progressively rise toward the chart's maximum. The bars are sorted sequentially by their block index rather than by ascending or descending value, and no individual bars are visually emphasized with special shading or outlines beyond their standard category colors.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity associated with a sequence of blocks, categorizing each block by a specific bit precision. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Block Index," which are arranged numerically from 0 to 63 with tick mark labels displayed at 0, 15, 31, 47, and 63. The vertical value axis is labeled "Sensitivity" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with dashed horizontal grid lines at $10^{-5}$ and $10^{-4}$, supplemented by unlabelled minor ticks denoting intermediate values. A legend in the upper left corner defines two color-coded categories: "4-Fbit" represented by blue bars and "2-Fbit" represented by green bars. Rather than grouping or stacking multiple categories at each position, the chart displays a single vertical bar for each block index, indicating its specific category. Green "2-Fbit" bars predominantly occupy the lower to middle indices, including a continuous stretch from index 0 to 27, and contain the shortest bar in the chart at index 5 with a value of approximately $2 \times 10^{-6}$. Blue "4-Fbit" bars are interspersed among the middle indices starting at index 28 and become contiguous toward the end of the sequence, displaying generally higher sensitivity values and culminating in the tallest bar at index 62, which reaches approximately $3 \times 10^{-4}$. The bars are sorted strictly by the numerical sequence of the Block Index rather than by height, and no specific bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or annotations beyond their standard category colors.
